forces.title: Connected TV Growth Shifts Content Consumption and Monetization
forces.description: The active Connected TV (CTV) base surged to 129.2 million users in 2025, with weekly active homes reaching 40 million, up from 30 million in 2024. While utilizing TV screens, CTV revenues are increasingly categorized under digital media. This structural shift alters how content is consumed and monetized, presenting a challenge for traditional TV broadcasting as revenue and audience engagement migrate to digitally-enabled TV platforms. This impacts both advertising and subscription models of IN040502.

forces.title: MSOs Bundling Broadband with Linear TV for Enhanced Offerings
forces.description: Cable multi-system operators (MSOs) are expected to innovate by bundling broadband services with linear TV feeds, integrating content aggregation apps and unified search capabilities. This proactive strategy is an upside driver for the TV broadcasting and cable industry, allowing MSOs to retain subscribers, attract new ones, and compete more effectively against pure-play OTT providers by offering a comprehensive digital entertainment package. This helps in evolving the traditional TV offering for modern consumers.

forces.title: Digital Media Overtakes TV as Largest M&E Segment
forces.description: In 2025, digital media surpassed television to become the largest segment within India's Media & Entertainment industry. This signifies a fundamental shift in revenue generation and audience engagement, with traditional TV's market dominance eroding as digital platforms capture a greater share of spending and consumption. This redefines competitive dynamics for TV broadcasters and cable operators, forcing adaptation to evolving consumer preferences and monetization models away from linear TV.

forces.title: Sports Media Rights Fragmenting Towards Digital Platforms
forces.description: The acquisition of IPL digital streaming rights by Viacom 18, while Star India secured TV broadcasting rights, exemplifies the fragmentation of premium sports media rights. Furthermore, for the 2025 IPL, digital platforms surpassed traditional TV in viewership. This represents a structural change, challenging linear TV's ability to offer exclusive, high-demand content and driving audiences towards digital streaming, impacting engagement and ad revenue potential for traditional broadcasters. This reduces key draw for linear TV subscriptions and viewership.

forces.title: Younger Viewers Shifting from Linear TV to Digital Platforms
forces.description: Younger audiences are increasingly shifting away from linear TV towards social platforms, gaming, and creator-driven content. They watch fewer minutes of traditional broadcasts and engage with content in new, fragmented ways, such as short clips and highlights. This fundamental change in viewership habits creates a significant headwind for traditional TV broadcasting, leading to audience erosion and reduced engagement, posing a long-term threat to sustaining future viewership and advertising appeal.

forces.title: Regional Content Growth on OTT Challenges Traditional TV
forces.description: Regional-language content's share on OTT platforms increased significantly from 27% in 2020 to 56% in 2025. This structural change, coupled with the rising popularity of dubbed and sub-titled content, means that a key differentiator for regional TV channels is now also thriving on digital platforms. This creates increased competition and may draw viewers away from traditional regional TV broadcasting, impacting their unique audience base and revenue generation, especially for smaller regional players.

forces.title: Declining Linear TV Ad Revenue Due to Digital Shift
forces.description: Linear TV advertising revenue declined by 10.3% in 2025, driven by decreased advertising volumes and a 3% reduction in advertisers. Sectors are shifting ad spend to digital media, particularly e-commerce and point-of-sale ads, which demonstrated better attribution. This trend represents a significant headwind for traditional TV broadcasters, impacting their primary revenue stream and necessitating strategic adaptation to retain advertising budgets. The shift reflects advertisers' preference for measurable digital outcomes.

forces.title: Loss of Pay TV Households Impacting Subscription Revenues
forces.description: Traditional Pay TV subscription revenues decreased by 8% in 2025, attributed to a loss of 11 million Pay TV households. Projections indicate a further fall of Linear Pay TV subscriptions by 3.1% to 83 million by 2028. This direct loss of subscribers poses a significant headwind, affecting both subscription income and the overall reach and appeal for advertisers within the TV broadcasting and cable industry. This decline signals a shift in consumer behavior towards alternative viewing options.

forces.title: High TV Reach Sustains Broad Audience Engagement
forces.description: Television continues to be the predominant medium in India, reaching approximately 745 million individuals each week. This extensive reach provides a significant tailwind for the TV broadcasting and cable industry, ensuring continued broad audience engagement despite shifts in viewership patterns. It maintains TV's relevance for advertisers seeking mass market exposure, especially in demographics or regions where digital media penetration is lower, offering a strong foundational audience.

forces.title: Increased FDI Limit Fosters Investment in Broadcasting Sector
forces.description: The Indian government's decision to increase the FDI limit from 74% to 100% in the information and broadcasting sector acts as a tailwind. This policy change is designed to attract greater foreign direct investment into the industry, potentially leading to increased capital infusion for technology upgrades, content production, and infrastructure development within TV broadcasting and cable operations, fostering overall growth and competitiveness by providing access to more funding.

viewpoints.title: Linear TV Remains Resilient, Transitioning to Lifestyle-Integrated Ecosystem
viewpoints.description: Kevin Vaz, Chairman of FICCI M&E Committee, views traditional media, including linear TV, as resilient despite evolving consumption patterns. He notes its transition from a regulated utility to a dynamic, lifestyle-integrated ecosystem that complements digital growth. This suggests a cautious positive outlook, implying that linear TV is adapting and maintaining its relevance by integrating with modern lifestyles and working alongside digital platforms, rather than being completely displaced. This perspective highlights adaptation over decline.

viewpoints.title: DTH Services Market Expected to Expand Moderately by 2029
viewpoints.description: India's Direct-To-Home (DTH) Services market is projected to grow from US$ 6.48 billion in 2023 to US$ 7.59 billion in 2029, exhibiting a CAGR of 2.8%. This moderate growth indicates continued, albeit not rapid, expansion for DTH operators within the broader TV broadcasting and cable sub-industry. The outlook suggests sustained demand for satellite-based television services in India, reflecting a cautious positive stance on this specific segment's future performance and stability.

viewpoints.title: Television Losing Ground to Digital Media as Primary M&E Segment
viewpoints.description: EY's report indicates that digital media has officially overtaken television as the largest segment of India's M&E industry in 2025. This structural shift highlights a negative trajectory for traditional television's market dominance, as advertising and subscription revenues continue to be impacted by the accelerated growth and market share capture of digital platforms, altering the industry landscape significantly. The shift suggests a sustained challenge for linear TV to maintain its leading position.

viewpoints.title: Digital Platforms Overtake TV in Major Sports Viewership, Signalling Shift
viewpoints.description: For the 2025 IPL, digital platforms surpassed traditional TV in viewership, drawing 652 million viewers compared to TV's 537 million. This marks a significant shift in audience preference for major sports events, driven by digital adoption and new features. This signals a negative outlook for linear TV's ability to retain exclusive large-scale event viewership, impacting advertising and engagement within the traditional broadcasting sector as high-value content migrates to digital.
